blocks.text: The C-X bond is polar because carbon and the halogen differ in electronegativity. The carbon of C-X is an electrophilic centre that a nucleophile can attack; alternatively, a hydrogen on the neighbouring carbon can be attacked by a base. These two possibilities give the two types of reaction of halogenoalkanes.

items: Nucleophilic substitution (SN): the halogen is replaced by another atom or group; the halide ion is the leaving group.
Elimination (E): HX is removed from the halogenoalkane, forming an alkene.

blocks.alt: Nu- with a curly arrow to the delta+ carbon of a substrate C-X (delta- on X), and a curly arrow from the C-X bond to X. The arrow gives Nu-C, with the other three bonds now on the opposite side, + X-. Labels: Attacking Nucleophile, Substrate Molecule, Substituted Product, Leaving Group.
